# Evaluation tooling

`scripts/eval_skill.py` uses standard-library Python. It validates cases, grades
existing artifacts and summarizes records; it never calls providers or executes
commands. Run from this skill's root or use the script's absolute path from any cwd.

## Cases and assertions

```bash
python3 scripts/eval_skill.py validate assets/eval-cases.example.json
python3 scripts/eval_skill.py validate /absolute/target-skill/evals/evals.json
```

Assertions have `id`, `text`, and optional `kind`:

| Kind | Required fields | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `file-exists` | `path` | Contained file exists |
| `json-equals` | `path`, `expected` | Parsed artifact matches expected JSON |
| `text-contains` | `path`, `expected` string | Required contract fragment exists |
| `rubric` (default) | `text` | Independent review with cited artifact evidence |

Use exact equality for machine contracts, not wording preferences. Paths are
relative to the output root; escaping paths and symlinks fail. Missing or malformed
artifacts fail. Rubric checks stay ungraded until reviewed. For richer checks,
run the existing domain verifier and retain its command, exit status and output.

## Run and grade

Discover available model runners and current flags from their help. Use a fresh
context with explicit output location. Do not assume provider credentials, model
names, isolation flags or delegation tools. If unavailable, record behavioral
verification as blocked and continue structural work with that limitation stated.

After an actual consumer run:

```bash
python3 scripts/eval_skill.py grade assets/eval-cases.example.json \
  --case-id normalize-valid --outputs /absolute/run/outputs \
  --run-id unique-session-id --variant candidate \
  --model effective-model-id --runtime observed-runtime-version \
  --skill /absolute/skill-snapshot > /absolute/run/record.json
```

No-skill: `--variant without_skill`, omit `--skill`. Other variants require a hash.
Optional observed metrics: `--tokens`, `--duration-ms`, `--tool-calls`, `--corrections`.
Omitted metrics stay null. For execution that did not complete, set `--status blocked`
or `--status failed` and retain the reason/provider error beside the record.

### Import observed configuration and usage

Add `--observations /absolute/run/observations.json` to `grade` to import a
provider-neutral evidence object. This file supplies observations only; it cannot
override run identity, skill hash, status or check verdicts. The parser in
`scripts/eval_contract.py` owns accepted fields and validation.

Illustrative shape (null means unavailable, not zero):

```json
{
  "effective_effort": null,
  "cache_state": null,
  "fingerprints": {
    "configuration": null, "cases": null, "tools": null, "catalog": null
  },
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": null, "output_tokens": null,
    "cache_read_tokens": null, "cache_write_tokens": null,
    "source": null, "semantics": null
  },
  "cost": {
    "amount": null, "currency": null, "source": null, "pricing_date": null
  },
  "loaded_references": null
}
```

Use observed effective effort rather than a requested alias. Fingerprints identify
the actual configuration, frozen cases, available tools and catalog; do not put raw
settings or secrets into records. `loaded_references: []` means the trace showed no
references read; null means reads were not observed. Usage source and semantics
describe how the runner mapped provider fields, including whether input includes
cached tokens. Do not sum fields using an assumed universal billing formula.

Cost records carry currency, evidence source and pricing date (YYYY-MM-DD).
Separate measured billing from an estimate in the source description; do not claim
actual savings from estimated or missing costs. Cache state is cold, warm, disabled
or null for unknown/mixed observations. Cold denotes no cached reads in the observed
span; disabled denotes no cache reads or writes. A session that starts cold and later
hits cache is mixed, not a cold-span record.

The importer neither changes model/effort nor operates provider caches. Use verified
runner controls for any authorized experiment, hold task conditions constant and
retain provider observations. Keep provider-specific caching recipes outside shared
skill instructions. Unknown metrics or unsupported providers remain explicit gaps.

Exit 0 means all checks passed (or valid cases/summary); 1 means failed, blocked or
ungraded; 2 means invalid input/configuration. Save records even on exit 1. Reviewers
may fill rubric verdicts with concrete evidence, preserving the original record
and reviewer identity separately.

```bash
python3 scripts/eval_skill.py summarize /absolute/run-a/record.json \
  /absolute/run-b/record.json > /absolute/comparison.json
```

Groups retain model, runtime, split, variant and hash; duplicate run ids fail.
Compare matching case sets, repetitions and conditions before interpreting deltas.
Summaries describe observations, not automatic promotion. Preserve redacted raw
outputs/traces. Missing metrics or uncovered targets never become zero-cost passes.

Extended groups also separate effort, cache state, fingerprints, usage semantics
and cost provenance. They expose `comparison_context`, `missing_evidence`,
`comparison_ready`, and per-metric observation counts. Incomplete extended records
remain separate runs; complete observations permit grouping, not a causal claim.
`observed_runs` retains reference reads per run, including null versus an observed
empty list. Reads are execution outcomes, so different paths through the same
assigned task/configuration remain visible within a group rather than splitting
matched repetitions. Inspect those outcomes and quality before interpreting means;
`comparison_ready` means the evidence fields are complete, not equal execution paths.
Legacy records still load and keep their previous aggregates, explicitly marked
without sufficient comparison evidence. Compare quality first and do not interpret
their aggregate tokens as a proven cost improvement.

## Optional catalog routing diagnostics

Use [semantic routing evaluation](semantic-routing-evaluation.md) only when explicitly
requested. Its separate script adds streaming probability diagnostics and trace-backed
runtime summaries; the commands above retain their offline behavior.
# Prompt Cruft Patterns
<!-- cruft-lint-allow: this file names the patterns the linter reports -->

Prompt cruft is instruction text whose cost or harm is supported by evidence on
the target consumers. This catalog identifies candidates for review; pattern
matches alone do not establish that a constraint is obsolete. Keep accepted
contracts and test behavior before removing guidance.

`scripts/lint_cruft.py` implements the signals below. It reports and never
edits. Rule ids in the table match the script's `--json` output.

## Classify by function before you judge

The same words mean different things in different places.

- **Routing text** (`description`, `when_to_use`, keyword lists) describes the
  owned task and activation boundary. With `--routing`, YAML-aware checks report
  advisory pressure and scope signals separately from body rules. A precise
  "whenever" condition is not itself a defect. Judge activation with real traces.
- **Behavioral text** (the SKILL.md body, references, agent bodies, output
  styles, hook text injected into context) must explain, not shout. Every
  rule below applies here.
- **Fragile scripts** (destructive commands, auth flows, compliance steps)
  keep their exact wording. Mark the block with `<!-- fragile -->` so the
  linter skips it.

## Pattern table

| Rule id | Level | Signal | Risk to investigate | Replacement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `routing-pressure` | Low | Metadata demands activation regardless of scope | Can crowd out a better matching skill | State owned work and activation conditions |
| `routing-keyword-scope` | Low | Activation tied to several generic keyword mentions | May include unrelated work; review against the competing catalog | Describe the actual task |
| `routing-metadata-format` | High | Invalid YAML or routing field types under `--routing` | Metadata cannot be inspected reliably | Repair metadata under the typed contract |
| `verification-ritual` | Low | Generic double-check or verify-twice instructions without a condition/reason | May duplicate successful checks | State completion evidence and when rechecking is needed |
| `approval-loop` | Medium | Approval or confirmation before/after each step or phase | Blanket checkpoints may ask again inside already-authorized scope; explicit interactive and destructive gates remain valid | Reuse authorization and ask for material missing decisions or new effects |
| `blanket-full-read` | Medium | Read all docs/references or the entire specification without a stated reason | Unconditional loading may hide the relevant contract inside unrelated context | Select the owning guide; preserve complete reads required by fragile operations |
| `fenced-reasoning` | Medium | `Thought N/M`, thinking tags, or requests to output internal reasoning in text/Markdown fences | Prompt examples may impose a transcript even when surrounding prose does not | Record decisions, observations and uncertainty; preserve exact fixtures with a scoped exemption |
| `pressure-density` | High at 8+ per file or 3 in any 10 lines; Medium at 4+ | MUST, NEVER, ALWAYS, CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, MANDATORY in body text | Stacked emphasis may over-trigger; test whether a protected instruction still needs emphasis | State the rule once at normal volume with its reason |
| `emphasis-no-reason` | Medium | A pressure word with no "because", "so that", or "otherwise" within two lines | Emphasis without a reason cannot be applied with judgment | Add the reason or drop the emphasis |
| `threat-language` | High | "INCOMPLETE", "DO NOT … yourself", "never skip", "MANDATORY —" | Threats produce compliance theatre (spawning agents for a typo fix) rather than judgment | Say when the step matters and why a fresh context helps |

docs/sandbox-spec.md:38:A recipe is self-contained when it relies on nothing but its own files, hyp and the subject, wherever its commands run. Self-contained does not mean "runs in the sandbox": a Standalone or scripted Evidence command is self-contained and runs with no sandbox. A fixed input that is not the subject, such as a fixture or a cases file, is a file of the bundle, so the recipe pin hashes it, and the code that reads it is in the bundle too. A file outside the bundle is the subject, or a read or write that the command's `External:` line names (ADR 0008, owner decision on 2026-11-01). hyp does not detect a fixture outside the bundle.
docs/sandbox-spec.md:40:Each Evidence and Standalone command states its reach on one line `External: TEXT` directly under its `Run:` line in `recipe.md`: the subject arguments and any outside reads or writes, or `none`. The line is no field `recipe.Load` requires, so a frozen bundle without it still loads and records. `hyp bundle check` warns `<command>: no External: line` for a command without one and `<command>: External: not stated (TODO)` for one whose text is empty or `TODO`, and exits as before. `hyp bundle new` writes `External: TODO` under each such command of a copy that has no line, and under the Standalone command of a first version. Every line of a first version's template that its author must replace holds the marker `hyp:placeholder`, and `hyp add exp --recipe` refuses (exit 1) a bundle that still holds it in any file outside a known answer's `input/`, naming the files (ADR 0009).
docs/sandbox-spec.md:129:- **Kept inputs.** An operator argument of `hyp bundle run` or `hyp bundle evidence`, alone or as the VALUE of a `KEY=VALUE` word, is a file argument when it is written as a path (absolute, or relative with a `/`; a relative one is read against the caller's directory) and names a regular file, symlinks followed. A bare word is never one, even when a file of that name exists. Before the first command runs, hyp copies each file argument N (ARGS counted from 1) under the run's temporary directory, which the script gets in its place, hashes that copy, and keeps a second copy beside the record at `DIR/inputs/N/<base name>`, so a script that writes to its argument changes neither the original nor the kept bytes. A file over 1 MB is not kept; its sha256 and size are. `command.json` (format 5) lists each in `inputs` (`arg`, `path`, `sha256`, `size`, `kept`), and the row shows `inputs/N/<base name>` in its place. A file inside the tree is copied too. A directory argument (such as Evidence's OUT_DIR) is passed as an absolute path and shown as `<repo>/REL`, `<repo>` being the directory name of the caller's git work tree (or of the caller's directory outside one); one outside it is shown as given, and hyp warns that a replay cannot reach it. hyp keeps no copy of a directory argument, but hashes its tree just before the first command runs and lists it in `dirs` (`arg`, `path`, `sha256`, `files`), so a record names the subject it judged. `path` and `cwd` are written the same way. So neither the record nor the `==` lines name a host path for anything a replay needs. The inputs are bound at run time, not when the Experiment is added (ADR 0008). Limits: a file the command reads without being given it is not kept; its `External:` line names it. A format-3 record's `arg_sha256` (each absolute file argument's sha256) is still read.

DesignQuestion Q-PC04ED
alias: q-commit
title: Which hyp commit implements the shared-store design?
path: G-D1CH1R > Q-PC04ED
status: answered
candidates: H-P4YGE2
selected: H-P4YGE2 — OWED owes this select: R-RRYBPH on 4047c01 (branch feat/one-subject-per-run) supports H-P4YGE2 under E-GAT8N4's rule and closed R-9SMRB2#4 and G-D1CH1R#1 to #8; #9 is accepted by the owner.
design: Commit 4047c01 on branch feat/one-subject-per-run, from 03e9e3d. Applies the owner's return of R-9SMRB2#4: ADR 0020 writes a run subject as {base, patch, files}, as the code, replay-spec and glossary do. The code (cmd/, internal/) is unchanged since b80d95d (git diff b80d95d 4047c01 -- cmd internal is empty), whose removal checks R-P1M8A8 logged.
limits:
  R-0HABWN#1 closed by R-CX1G1C (H-P65RW9 (one-subject-per-arm) supports) — F1: a sandbox record with two --patch Arms at base B is kept as one run subject {B, [pa, pb]}, so a Hypothesis tied to B plus Arm a's patch is never covered though that Arm ran at B; a subject has at most one patch.
  R-0HABWN#2 accepted by owner-dat — F2: line 3's new tests fail to build on 9429fc1, so neither half fails on the commit before its change with a message naming its rule (line 9's case for line 3).
  R-0HABWN#3 closed by R-CX1G1C (H-P65RW9 (one-subject-per-arm) supports) — F3: no test runs rule 26 on a base: a bare-B subject re-tied after a run at B plus a patch must be admitted, and refused with 'subject ran in' after a run at exactly B.
  R-0HABWN#4 closed by R-CX1G1C (H-P65RW9 (one-subject-per-arm) supports) — F4: a Hypothesis tied with --base B and two paths of the same bytes is never held, because run files are unique by sha256 and subject files unique by path.
  R-0HABWN#5 closed by R-CX1G1C (H-P65RW9 (one-subject-per-arm) supports) — F5: hyp subject --base exits 2 when git is not on PATH; a missing tool is an environment problem, exit 3.
  R-0HABWN#6 closed by R-CX1G1C (H-P65RW9 (one-subject-per-arm) supports) — F6: replay admits a Result whose subjects are not empty while its evidence is empty, though subjects are copied only from cited records.
  R-0HABWN#7 closed by R-7XVMDC (H-W35076 supports) — Q: a sandbox run at B with an --inputs file never covers a Hypothesis whose subject is bare B, because a based subject is held only by a run given exactly its files.
  R-9SMRB2#1 closed by R-Q9WTZB (H-JA5S86 contradicts), R-KBW141 (H-AX7M2K supports) — F1: a Hypothesis tied to B plus arm.patch is covered by a run at bare B with no Arm whose --inputs file has the patch's bytes, though the patch never changed the code.
  R-9SMRB2#2 closed by R-Q9WTZB (H-JA5S86 contradicts), R-KBW141 (H-AX7M2K supports) — F2: a Hypothesis tied to B plus an input file I is held by a run at B whose patch is I, because a Hypothesis's subject does not say which of its files is the patch.
  R-9SMRB2#3 closed by R-Q9WTZB (H-JA5S86 contradicts), R-KBW141 (H-AX7M2K supports) — F3: replay-spec rule 27 still names 'a subject with no base and no files' and not the new 'no base, no patch and no files' or 'patch ... is not a sha256' rejections.
  R-9SMRB2#4 closed by R-RRYBPH (H-P4YGE2 supports) — F4: ADR 0020 still writes a run subject as {base, files} with no patch field, while the code, replay-spec and glossary write {base, patch, files}.
  R-9SMRB2#5 accepted by owner-dat — F5: a Result written by a 7257753 or 3ec4979 binary keeps an Arm's patch inside files, so 0cda2f8 replays it as a run at B given input P, which covers bare B.
  R-9SMRB2#6 closed by R-Q9WTZB (H-JA5S86 contradicts), R-KBW141 (H-AX7M2K supports) — F6: no test runs rule 26 after the owner's case: once a run at B given inputs holds a bare-B Hypothesis, a new tie of that Hypothesis must be refused with 'subject ran in'.
  R-9SMRB2#7 accepted by owner-dat — Q: a sandbox with Arms keeps only patched subjects, so a bare-B control its Launch builds gives no bare-B subject, and a bare-B Hypothesis stays uncovered by it.
  R-3EN4FB#1 closed by R-P1M8A8 (H-71PQR7 supports) — G1: a sandbox.json Arm whose sha256 is not lowercase hex is kept as a run at bare B with no patch, so that patched run covers a Hypothesis whose subject is bare B.
  R-3EN4FB#2 closed by R-P1M8A8 (H-71PQR7 supports) — G2: hyp subject H arm.patch --base B --patch arm.patch is admitted, with one path as both the patch and an input, so a run at B plus that Arm never covers H.
  R-3EN4FB#3 closed by R-P1M8A8 (H-71PQR7 supports) — G3: replay-spec rule 28 says a records path named twice is refused with 'bad subject: <path> listed twice', while the code says 'bad records: <path> named twice'.
  R-3EN4FB#4 closed by R-P1M8A8 (H-71PQR7 supports) — G4: replay-spec section 6 writes the projection's Subjects as a map to []SubjectFile, while the code holds a HypothesisSubject, so the spec cannot show a subject's base or patch.

I ran `hyp init` at a repo root that already had a nested store. - **Fixtures** are fabricated. The flow allows only fabricated or approved redacted fixtures. They are a synthetic store with one Goal whose body ends in a strict constraints block, plus a golden prompt file. The golden is the run-5 prompt from the issue, with its placeholders, and its sha256 goes in the line.

- **Binary lines** are decided by `go test`. AGENTS.md makes that the gate for refusals and warnings, so it is not a choice.
- **Skill edits** follow the eval flow. Cases go in `evals.json` format, kept in a `recipes/<skill>-eval@N` bundle. Test agents run on Sonnet, 3 trials, comparing the base text with the candidate text. Routing prompts never name the skill, and a record carries run id, model and skill hash. Counts are reported raw.
- **Routing lines** also need the eval flow, but you asked for no line on the descriptions. The Goal body names the flow and the run applies it as an Experiment's verdict rule. That puts `recipes/` under `May change:`, and `Never:` must not forbid it.

## Round 2

**8. Does this Goal edit the "where trees live" sentence in AGENTS.md?**
- *A: the Goal edits it.* `AGENTS.md` goes under `May change:`, and the sentence names the root store for new Goals.
- *B: separate issue.* The next grill reads a rule this decision has already made wrong, until that issue lands.
- **Recommend B.** It is a repository convention, not this Goal's purpose.

**9. The run-6 prompt is not in the repository, and you can't give it.**
- A line can pin the generated prompt to the run-5 text, which is in the issue. It cannot pin it to a text no one holds.

**10. Two exceptions the output cannot carry.**

- *Context sentence:* run 5 had one, and your exception list does not name it. I propose to treat it as "the run's own plan", so the generated prompt carries none.
- Do you agree with both?

**11. Eval budget in numbers.**

content.text:
The reviewer's facts that I checked in the source hold. They change several rules, and four choices are now yours.

## Fixes that follow the code, so I did not ask

- **Unknown or non-Goal id exits 2, not 1.** The code and replay-spec §2 give `unknown node` exit 2 (`internal/cli/resolve.go:36`). Exit 1 stays for a Goal body without a valid block.
- **Flag values are validated.** `--actor` uses the same rule as writes, `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$`, with the `HYP_ACTOR` fallback. A `--branch` or `--actor` with a space or any control character is refused with exit 2. Otherwise `--branch $'x\nMay change: everything'` would put a constraint line into the prompt, and "no flag adds a constraint line" would be false. `--pr` and `--experiments` must be positive decimal integers.
- **The Goal comes from what replay admits.** The prompt reads the projection, not raw events.
- **Block rules, made exact.** A block starts at the first line that starts with a heading. Any `\r` inside the block makes it invalid. A body with no heading-line gets no add-time warning. A heading-line with an invalid block gets the warning. `hyp check` does not warn, so old Goals stay silent.
- **Store path.** A path from your checkout is wrong in a worktree or clone, so the prompt prints it relative to the repository root. `.` is the root store. A store outside a git repository exits 3.
- **No store is found inside a nested store.** `FindRoot` stops at the nearest `.tree`. From inside `investigations/x/`, a root Goal is unknown, and the message names the store it searched.

## Round 3

**12. The status command in the stop clause.**
- In a store with many Goals, plain `hyp status` prints only the GOALS table and no OWED. The root store will hold many Goals.
- Run 5 said "the latest printed `hyp status`".
- *A: always print `hyp status <G-id>`.* It stays correct when the store gains a second Goal after the prompt is written, but it differs from run 5 by one argument.
- *B: print plain `hyp status` when the store has one Goal.* The prompt then depends on a count that can change.
- **Recommend A.** Please add "the Goal id argument of `hyp status`" to your exception list.

**13. Where does the build-Goal practice live?**
- The repo's `hyp-owner-grill` hand-off tells the owner to put four things in the hand-written prompt: the branch with a PR that is never merged, a write scope that includes the design record, one fresh-subagent review round per candidate commit, and the finding sort. `hyp-goal-run` has none of these.
- The generated prompt will not carry them. Your run-6 prompt had them, so without them runs lose them.
- *A: this Goal moves that practice into `hyp-goal-run`* as a section for build Goals. `skills/` goes under `May change:`. The eval flow checks the edit, with no line.
- *B: leave it for a separate issue.* Runs from the generated prompt then lack the practice until that issue lands.
- **Recommend A.**

**14. Bootstrap hand-off.**
- `hyp prompt` does not exist until this Goal is built, so I can't print the hand-off with it.
- I would give you a hand-written prompt in the shape the grill skill describes, labelled as not hyp's output. The skill says to give the owner hyp's output as it is.
- Do you accept that once?

**15. Is "binary or skill-written prompt" recorded as a DesignQuestion?**
- Issue #113 leaves both open.
- A run could separate them. The scenarios are an invalid block, two Goals in one store, and byte-identical output across three runs.
- A decided DesignQuestion in this build Goal would owe every line forever, because a skill-written rival cannot be run against the exit-code lines.
- *A: a second Goal in the same root store, a design record with no lines.* It holds the DesignQuestion, two rivals, and a runner Experiment `--recipe none --rubric reading` with the scenarios file. Your answers in this session are the evidence, and the runner records the select.
- *B: not recorded.* AGENTS.md's rule already puts failures detectable from the tree into the binary.
- **Recommend A.** The tree then says it was argued, not tested.

## Draft lines for the build Goal

Baseline for the lines that compare output is the binary built from `a51f140` with AGENTS.md's build command. Its sha256 is `acd9b417627e9b773156b9c2a758a1becfccd3280f1ff1adfe1e5cb8e3687586`. Two builds here gave the same hash. On it, `hyp prompt` exits 2 with the usage screen.

| # | | Invariant |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [P] | On a fixture store with one Goal and a valid block, `hyp prompt G --actor A` exits 0 and prints the run-5 prompt clause for clause. Only these differ: actor, Goal id, store path, the block lines, the `hyp status` argument, and no owner answer, plan, context sentence or commit. The base binary's output differs. |
| 2 | [P] | `--experiments N` changes only the count (default 5). `--branch` and `--pr` each add one clause after the block that grants nothing. No flag changes, removes or adds a constraint line. |
| 3 | [N] | A body with no heading-line, a missing heading, or a non-empty non-heading line in the block (a space-only, tab or `\r` line counts as non-empty) is refused with exit 1, nothing on stdout, and a message naming what is missing or the first bad line. |
| 4 | [N] | Bad arguments are refused before the store is read, with exit 2 and a message naming the argument. This covers an invalid actor, a `--branch` with a space or control character, a non-integer `--pr` or `--experiments`, and a missing actor. |
| 5 | [N] | An unknown, ambiguous or non-Goal id exits 2. No store exits 3. A store outside a git repository exits 3. |
| 6 | [N] | In a store with two Goals, one Goal's prompt never includes the other's id, lines or block. It equals what its own events give in a store of their own. |
| 7 | [N] | `hyp prompt` writes nothing: `.tree/` is byte-identical before and after, and two runs print the same bytes. |
| 8 | [P] | `hyp add goal` with a heading-line but an invalid block exits 0, writes the node, and warns naming what is missing. With no heading-line it exits 0 with no warning. `hyp check` on the four `investigations/` stores prints the same bytes as the base binary. |

Lines 3, 4 and 5 are refusals of a read command, so they have no "rejected on replay" half. No log can hold the forbidden state, because no event is written.

## Routing table, to confirm after 12 to 15

| Question | Goes to | Scenario or invariant |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose, scope, why | Goal title and body | none |
| Lines 1 to 8 | the Goal's lines | as in the table above |
| Constraints | body: `May change:` the repo's `cmd/`, `internal/`, `skills/`, `docs/`, `README.md` and a new `recipes/` eval bundle, as commits on the branch the prompt names. `Read only:` the four `investigations/` stores, ak-skill-creator's `eval_skill.py`, and the text of #113. `Never:` merge a PR, replace the installed binary, edit the AGENTS.md sentence on where trees live, or put real source data in the repo | none |
| Run-6 match cannot be checked | body sentence; a new issue holds the unmet half | none |
| Skill description wording | no line; `skills/` under `May change:` | none |
| How skill edits are tested | body names ak-skill-creator's flow: 24 Sonnet runs (4 cases × 2 variants × 3 trials), routing prompts never name the skill | none |
| Binary or skill-written prompt | DQ with two rivals in a second Goal (design record, no lines), if you take 15 A | invalid block, two Goals, byte-identical across three runs |
| Which commit builds it | the build Goal's one DQ, with no rivals at the grill; the run adds the commit Hypotheses | none |
| AGENTS.md "where trees live" | another Goal or issue | named |
| Looked up, not asked | exit codes, flag validation, store path form, projection source | from the code |

Constraint wording for AGENTS.md is the one sentence on where trees live, not the file. If that sentence is not the only AGENTS.md text this change makes wrong, the run can't fix the rest. Tell me if you want `AGENTS.md` under `May change:` with that sentence excluded instead.

The Goal body must fit 2000 runes, because `MaxGoalBody` is 2000. I will show the exact body and every write command with `owner-standin` for your approval before running them.
